subject.title: Adding ACP agent to agents.list silently hijacks all routing from implicit main agent

question: Should a populated `agents.list` without `default: true` keep using the first listed agent as the global fallback, or should OpenClaw preserve implicit `main` until the user explicitly chooses a new default?
rationale: Current docs and source encode first-entry default behavior, but the issue shows that behavior can silently move session state, message routing, and security boundaries; changing it affects existing multi-agent installs and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve implicit main unless default is explicit
options.body: Make `main` remain the fallback when `agents.list` is introduced without `default: true`, and add doctor/config guidance for users who intended the first listed agent to become global default.

options.title: Keep first-entry default with stronger warnings
options.body: Retain current routing semantics but make `openclaw config set`, doctor, and docs warn loudly when a first `agents.list` write displaces implicit `main`.

options.title: Require explicit default for non-empty lists
options.body: Fail or warn on non-empty `agents.list` without exactly one default, trading upgrade friction for unambiguous routing.

recommendation.title: Preserve implicit main unless default is explicit
recommendation.body: Make `main` remain the fallback when `agents.list` is introduced without `default: true`, and add doctor/config guidance for users who intended the first listed agent to become global default.
